Note: the slots are flat recesses to hold strips against the face — a true through-slot pocket that captures a strip's edges from behind isn't something I can machine here.

declined.what: CAFE following a true curved arc baseline (each letter rotated along the arc)
declined.why: text sits on a straight baseline — I can't set rotated/arced letterforms, so CAFE is engraved straight across the top; I authored an arc guide shape you could bore along, but the letters themselves stay level.

prompt: A big teaching protractor, semicircle with degree tick marks every 5 degrees engraved around the arc and numbers at every 10.

payload.summary: Built a large teaching protractor: a semicircular disc with engraved tick marks every 5° around the arc (longer at every 10°) and numbers engraved every 10° — I authored the 0–180 numbers as individual placed labels around the arc, and added a small hang hole; say the word to drop it.

prompt: A little TIPS sign frame that sits on the counter, engraved lettering, with a slot to drop coins into a jar behind it.

payload.summary: Built a countertop TIPS sign: V-carved editable lettering up top, a rounded coin slot cut through below it to drop coins into a jar behind, and a rounded-rectangle plaque cut free with holding tabs; the slot width is on a slider.

declined.what: an integrated stand/easel so the frame stands upright on its own
declined.why: I only cut flat panels — a fold-out or A-frame stand would need furniture-style joined panels, so this is a single flat plaque you'd prop with a small stand or lean against the jar

prompt: Angled business card holder, front lip and a back that leans at about 15 degrees, holds a stack of cards, our logo area engraved on front.

payload.summary: Built an angled business-card holder as flat-panel furniture — a base, two full-height sides, a low front lip that captures the card stack, and a back panel that leans ~15° (Back lean slider), with your text V-carved on the front lip; the front stops at the lip height so cards angle back against the tilted rear.

prompt: Fraction teaching circles — a whole, halves, thirds, quarters, and eighths — each circle cut into the right number of wedge pieces.

payload.summary: Built a Fraction Circles app: pick the diameter and how many pieces (whole/halves/thirds/quarters/eighths) and it cuts that many radial wedges plus the disc — but I need to flag a geometry problem with how the wedge cuts are laid out, see below.

prompt: A name tracing board with the letters of a kid's name grooved so they can run a stylus through the channel, like OLIVIA.

payload.summary: Built a name-tracing board that engraves a kid's name as single-line grooved channels (default "OLIVIA") for a stylus to follow, then cuts the board free as a rounded tag.

prompt: A number line teaching ruler, 600mm, with tick marks and numbers 0 to 20 engraved along a straight scored line.

payload.summary: Started a 600 mm number-line ruler — but I need to fix how the scored line, ticks, and 0–20 numbers are actually cut before this is right; see the note.

prompt: A set of periodic table element tiles, each 40mm square with the symbol, atomic number, and name engraved. Just the first 20 elements.

payload.summary: Built a 40mm-square element tile that engraves the atomic number (top-left), symbol (large, center), and name (below), all bound to editable controls — retype the three fields for each of the first 20 elements (H, He, Li, … Ca) and add each verified tile to your Current board to run the whole set from one sheet.
